issues.parameter: component masses, mass ratio, donor radius and geometry
issues.competing_evidence: Borisov+15 primary abstract reports M1=0.75±0.02 Msun, M2=0.16±0.01 Msun, q=0.21±0.02, RL2=0.18±0.02 Rsun; full article inaccessible and q convention/method cannot be checked. Kolbin+22 full text applies irradiated-line correction K2=390±11 km/s (assumed donor Teff=3250 K, log g=5, Lx=1e32), Roche filling and donor inflation k=1.15 to derive Q=M1/M2=5.12±0.35, i=85±0.5, M1=0.60±0.04, M2≈0.116, R2=0.155; separate stream tomography gives Q≈6.5 and conflicts with the eclipse solution.
issues.why_it_matters: Masses and mass ratio shape component comparisons and any evolutionary interpretation; later values are model-dependent and the same paper has inconsistent Q fits.
issues.needed_action: Obtain Borisov+15 full paper to check q convention, velocity treatment and assumptions; compare irradiation corrections/tomography or seek an independent RV/eclipsing solution. Retain both sets without averaging or declaring one uniquely measured.

issues.competing_evidence: Denisenko+06 eclipse timing 96.264±0.0288 min; Borisov+15 value quoted by Kolbin+22 96.308701056±0.000000288 min; Hernández-Díaz+25 TESS LS candidate 96.30260±0.00240 min. TESS differs by 0.366 s (2.54 formal TESS errors if treated alone), but Tmag=17.591 is in that paper’s uncertain reliability range and BS Tri is among 85/95 deemed consistent under the sample-wide comparison. Kolbin+22 say old ephemerides failed because of timing/support issues; no Pdot established.
issues.why_it_matters: Period/ephemeris choices affect eclipse cycle counts and future spin/beat interpretation; faint TESS period has limited source-level reliability.
issues.needed_action: Inspect full Borisov+15 ephemeris and TESS periodogram/sectors; acquire fresh timed eclipses or independent multi-epoch timings before changing the scalar period or claiming Pdot. Keep each result separately pending verification.

references.note: Local PDF/text and arXiv record inspected for BS Tri. MNRAS 511, 20-30. Reports P_orb=0.0668810424(2) d from Borisov+15, Q=5.12 +/-0.35, i=85 +/-0.5 deg, M1=0.60 +/-0.04 Msun, M2=0.116 (~0.12) Msun, R1=0.0125 +/-0.0005 Rsun, R2=0.155 Rsun, accretion-spot cyclotron B=22.7 +/-0.4 MG with Te~7.5 keV, H-alpha Zeeman cool-halo feature B=21.5 +/-1 MG, and assumed irradiated-donor atmosphere Teff=3250 K/logg=5.0. No measured WD photospheric Teff or donor spectral subtype found. Rechecked full text: corrected irradiated-donor K2=390±11 km/s and f(M)=0.411±0.003 Msun. Eclipse/evolutionary-radius model (Roche filling, donor inflation factor 1.15) gives Q=M1/M2=5.12±0.35, i=85±0.5 deg, M1=0.60±0.04 Msun, M2≈0.116 Msun (no formal uncertainty), R1=0.0125±0.0005 Rsun, R2=0.155 Rsun and a=0.62±0.01 Rsun; separate stream tomography gives Q≈6.5 and conflicts with the eclipse solution. Teff=3250 K/log g=5 and Lx=1e32 erg/s are assumed inputs to irradiation corrections. Halpha Zeeman features are assigned to a cool halo near the accretion spot, not WD photosphere. No WD Teff, cooling age, moment or global WD field found.
